text: 227 of the 3,144 US counties and county equivalents have no private law office and no self-employed legal business on record.
textEs: 227 de los 3,144 condados y equivalentes de Estados Unidos no tienen ningún despacho de abogados privado ni ningún negocio legal por cuenta propia registrado.
limits: Law offices are BLS establishment counts for 2026 Q1; self-employed businesses are the Census nonemployer count (NES 2024). Lawyers in a neighboring county, government lawyers and legal aid are not counted.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

denominatorLabel: counties with no private law office
text: 235 of the 293 counties with no private law office had at least one death in a truck or bus crash from 2016 to 2025, 1,357 deaths in all.
textEs: 235 de los 293 condados sin despacho de abogados privado tuvieron al menos una muerte en un choque de camión o autobús entre 2016 y 2025, 1,357 muertes en total.
limits: Crashes are those reported to FMCSA (federally reportable truck and bus crashes), counted in the county where the crash happened, not where the people lived. A county with no law office can still be served from a nearby town.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: percent of residents aged 5 and over who speak Spanish at home
text: 13.6% of US residents aged 5 and over speak Spanish at home, but only 5.2% of lawyers, judges and judicial workers do (67,037 of 1,284,045).
textEs: El 13.6% de los residentes de Estados Unidos de 5 años o más habla español en casa, pero solo el 5.2% de los abogados, jueces y trabajadores judiciales lo hace (67,037 de 1,284,045).
limits: American Community Survey 2020-2024 estimates with margins of error. The census occupation group includes judges and court workers, and speaking Spanish at home does not mean practicing law in Spanish.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: 20 of 51 jurisdictions make lawyers wait a set time before sending targeted contact to people after an accident or injury.
textEs: 20 de 51 jurisdicciones obligan a los abogados a esperar un plazo fijo antes de contactar directamente a personas después de un accidente o una lesión.
limits: The length and reach differ by state: some cover only written contact, some only certain accidents or disasters. Each state page quotes the rule. Not legal advice.
confidenceBasis: one primary source, no second check

text: Only seven of 51 jurisdictions make lawyers file their ads with a bar or court office, and Florida charges the most, $250 per ad.
textEs: Solo siete de 51 jurisdicciones obligan a los abogados a presentar sus anuncios ante un colegio de abogados o un tribunal, y Florida cobra la tarifa más alta, $250 por anuncio.
limits: Counts states where advertisements in general must be filed; a few more require filing only for targeted solicitations. Fees are the standard per-ad fee before late or rush fees.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: Truck and bus crashes reported to federal safety regulators killed 4,579 people in 2025, about 13 a day, in 4,114 fatal crashes.
textEs: Los choques de camiones y autobuses reportados a la autoridad federal de seguridad mataron a 4,579 personas en 2025, unas 13 al día, en 4,114 choques mortales.
limits: FMCSA's crash file holds federally reportable crashes involving a truck or bus; late reports can still be added. NHTSA's FARS counts large-truck crashes a different way.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: Retaliation was named in 54,350 of the 88,201 charges filed with the EEOC in fiscal year 2025 (61.6%), more than any other basis.
textEs: Las represalias aparecieron en 54,350 de los 88,201 cargos presentados ante la EEOC en el año fiscal 2025 (61.6%), más que cualquier otro motivo.
limits: A charge can name more than one basis, so the bases add up to more than the total. Charges are allegations, not findings, and state and local agencies take more.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

denominatorLabel: completions a month this fiscal year
text: Immigration courts had 3,469,569 cases pending on June 30, 2026, about 47 months of work at this fiscal year’s pace of 73,371 completed cases a month.
textEs: Los tribunales de inmigración tenían 3,469,569 casos pendientes el 30 de junio de 2026, unos 47 meses de trabajo al ritmo de este año fiscal, 73,371 casos terminados al mes.
limits: EOIR counts are preliminary and subject to change. The months figure divides the backlog by the current pace; it is not a forecast, since new cases keep arriving and the pace changes.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: In fiscal year 2025, 119,519 of 263,133 completed immigration court cases had no representative on record (45.4%).
textEs: En el año fiscal 2025, 119,519 de 263,133 casos terminados en los tribunales de inmigración no tenían representante registrado (45.4%).
limits: EOIR leaves out in absentia orders, terminations and dismissals from this count. A representative can be a lawyer or an accredited representative.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: 2,333 of 3,135 counties have no VA-accredited attorney or claims agent with a business address there, and about 4,066,000 veterans live in them.
textEs: 2,333 de 3,135 condados no tienen ningún abogado ni agente de reclamaciones acreditado por el VA con dirección comercial allí, y en ellos viven unos 4,066,000 veteranos.
limits: Counted by business address on the VA lists; an accredited attorney or agent can help a veteran anywhere. Veterans service organizations’ representatives are not counted, and veteran counts are VA projections.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: percent of attorney-represented Legacy appeals allowed
text: In fiscal year 2024, the Board of Veterans’ Appeals allowed 42.7% of 14,500 Legacy appeals with an attorney and 29.7% of 4,544 with no representative.
textEs: En el año fiscal 2024, la Junta de Apelaciones de Veteranos concedió el 42.7% de 14,500 apelaciones Legacy con abogado y el 29.7% de 4,544 sin representante.
limits: Board-wide counts of decided Legacy-system appeals. They do not show that representation changed the outcome: the cases each group brings can differ in many ways.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: The general deadline to sue for a personal injury runs from 1 year in Kentucky and Tennessee to 6 years in Maine, Minnesota and North Dakota, across 51 jurisdictions.
textEs: El plazo general para demandar por lesiones personales va de 1 año en Kentucky y Tennessee a 6 años en Maine, Minnesota y Dakota del Norte, en 51 jurisdicciones.
limits: The general rule only: car-crash, discovery, minor, government-claim and other exceptions can change a deadline. Not legal advice; a lawyer in the state decides a real deadline.
confidenceBasis: secondary status, official source

unit: percent change, consumer price index for legal services
text: Consumer prices for legal services rose 47.3% from January 2017 to September 2026, against 38.8% for all items.
textEs: Los precios al consumidor de los servicios legales subieron 47.3% de enero de 2017 a septiembre de 2026, frente a 38.8% en todos los artículos.
limits: The consumer index follows a basket of household legal services such as wills, divorces and closings. It is not a law firm’s billing rate, and BLS does not seasonally adjust it.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: percent change, producer price index for offices of lawyers
text: The prices law offices receive for their work rose 62.9% from January 2017 to September 2026, faster than the 47.3% rise in what households pay for legal services.
textEs: Los precios que reciben las oficinas de abogados por su trabajo subieron 62.9% de enero de 2017 a septiembre de 2026, más que el 47.3% que subió lo que pagan los hogares por servicios legales.
limits: The producer price index covers all of law offices’ work, mostly for businesses. The latest month is preliminary and BLS revises it for four months.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: percent of employer law firms’ receipts
text: The 203 law firms with 500 or more employees were 0.13% of the 156,583 employer law firms in 2022 but took in 34.9% of their receipts.
textEs: Los 203 bufetes con 500 empleados o más eran el 0.13% de los 156,583 bufetes con empleados en 2022, pero recibieron el 34.9% de sus ingresos.
limits: Census Statistics of US Businesses: employer firms only, sized by their employees nationwide. Self-employed lawyers with no staff are counted separately and are not in either figure.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: actions pending in the largest docket
denominatorLabel: actions pending in 162 open MDL dockets
text: On October 1, 2026, one docket, MDL-2738 (Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder), held 33.8% of the 204,977 actions pending in 162 open multidistrict litigation dockets.
textEs: El 1 de octubre de 2026, un solo expediente, el MDL-2738 (Johnson & Johnson Talcum Powder), reunía el 33.8% de las 204,977 acciones pendientes en 162 expedientes de litigio multidistrito abiertos.
limits: From the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation’s pending-dockets report. An action is a case, and one case can hold more than one plaintiff.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: months, longest average wait from hearing request to hearing
text: For Social Security disability cases closed in August 2026, the average wait from hearing request to hearing ran from 7.0 months in 14 offices to 12.0 months in Phoenix North, AZ, across 158 hearing offices.
textEs: En los casos de discapacidad del Seguro Social cerrados en agosto de 2026, la espera promedio entre la solicitud de audiencia y la audiencia fue de 7.0 meses en 14 oficinas a 12.0 meses en Phoenix North, AZ, entre 158 oficinas de audiencias.
limits: SSA’s monthly averages for cases closed that month, by hearing office; one month can move with a few cases. The national review unit is left out.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

denominatorLabel: cases filed in the 12 months before
text: 621,111 bankruptcy cases were filed in the 12 months ending September 30, 2026, up 11.4% from 557,376 a year earlier.
textEs: Se presentaron 621,111 casos de bancarrota en los 12 meses que terminaron el 30 de septiembre de 2026, un aumento del 11.4% frente a 557,376 un año antes.
limits: US Courts table F-2: cases commenced, business and nonbusiness, all chapters. A filing by a married couple counts once.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

text: Federal regulators fined 6,468 of the 14,686 certified nursing homes (44.0%) from October 2023 to September 2026, $445.7 million in all.
textEs: La autoridad federal multó a 6,468 de los 14,686 hogares de ancianos certificados (44.0%) entre octubre de 2023 y septiembre de 2026, $445.7 millones en total.
limits: CMS penalty records as published on Care Compare, which keeps about three years. A fine is a federal enforcement action, not a court finding of abuse or neglect.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources

unit: dollars of FLSA overtime back wages found owed
denominatorLabel: dollars of back wages found owed, fiscal years 2016 to 2025
text: From fiscal year 2016 to 2025, the Labor Department’s Wage and Hour Division found $2.09 billion in back wages owed to 1,732,370 employees, and unpaid overtime was 61.8% of it ($1.29 billion).
textEs: De los años fiscales 2016 a 2025, la División de Salarios y Horas del Departamento de Trabajo encontró $2.09 mil millones en salarios atrasados adeudados a 1,732,370 empleados, y las horas extra no pagadas fueron el 61.8% ($1.29 mil millones).
limits: Cases the Division concluded with findings, from the Labor Department’s public enforcement file; recent years still fill in as cases close. Private lawsuits and state agencies’ recoveries are not counted, and back wages found owed are not always paid.
confidenceBasis: primary source; checked within 105 days; two primary sources
